outcome: The owner-promoted same-minute Pay failure is repaired: an accepted native payment can now transition its committed shakedown to returning_home without changing the ordinary same-minute transition rule.  The normal first-contact gate now also opens parley when a nearby follower, rather than the player, first sights an active bandit; rolling travel remains the explicit ambush exception.
summary: The narrow source change allows only committed_contact -> returning_home, at equality with the reservation cursor, when the caller explicitly identifies the paid-return path.  Separately, the local gate now accumulates nearby-follower sight while examining the active outing and uses it solely for normal first-sight parley eligibility; it neither contributes follower goods nor changes rolling-travel ambush behavior.  A source-bound native run opened the trade UI, paid the 18,724-cent demand with a $193.20 coin stack, recorded `shakedown_trade_ui result=paid` and `shakedown_surface paid ... return=physical`, and saved the exact operation in returning_home with members 18 and 19.  A fresh post-relaunch run a8dad951e2b94932a7c1a0d64a4885f6 used the saved world, advanced 120 ordinary turns, and has four green step-local records: native World bootstrap, deferred ordinary-turn proof, no resumed member-18/19 fight path, and clean feature debug guard.  The focused current-source test set passes 195 assertions in four cases, including the bounded Pay/Fight surface, terminal receipt/aftermath, renegotiation pressure, and bandit-loss cooling.  OCR, terminal text, and presentation were not used as proof.  The post-relaunch-only classifier is yellow `inconclusive_no_artifact_match` because it deliberately has no same-run positive payment artifact; its local continuation proof is green and the payment evidence is retained in the preceding source-bound run.
